text: A light-year measures distance, not time - it's the distance light travels in one year.
Saturn's rings are made mostly of ice particles, with a smaller amount of rocky debris.
A day on Venus is longer than its year, because it rotates so slowly on its axis.
Neutron stars are so dense that a teaspoon of their material would weigh billions of tons.
The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at a rate of about 3.8 centimeters per year.
Searing meat at high heat creates a browned crust through the Maillard reaction, adding flavor.
Baking soda and baking powder are not interchangeable - baking powder already contains an acid.
Resting meat after cooking allows the juices to redistribute instead of spilling out when cut.
Blanching vegetables briefly in boiling water then ice water helps them keep a bright color.
Adding salt to pasta water raises its boiling point only slightly, but it seasons the pasta itself.
In tennis, a 'love' score means zero points, likely derived from the French word for egg, 'l'oeuf'.
A marathon's official distance, 26.2 miles, was standardized for the 1908 London Olympics.
In basketball, the shot clock forces a team to attempt a shot within a fixed number of seconds.
Offside in soccer depends on a player's position relative to the ball and the last defender.
A perfect game in bowling requires twelve consecutive strikes for a score of 300.
A major scale follows the interval pattern whole-whole-half-whole-whole-whole-half.
A tritone splits an octave exactly in half and was historically called 'the devil's interval.'
Syncopation places emphasis on beats that aren't normally stressed, creating a sense of surprise.
A key signature tells a musician which notes are consistently sharp or flat throughout a piece.
A perfect cadence resolves from the dominant chord back to the tonic, giving a sense of finality.
Mount Everest's summit sits at about 8,849 meters, the highest point on Earth's surface above sea level.
The Mariana Trench plunges to roughly 11,000 meters, the deepest known point in any ocean.
Death Valley reaches temperatures near 57 degrees Celsius, among the hottest recorded air temperatures on Earth.
The Sahara spans over 9 million square kilometers, making it the largest hot desert in the world.
Lake Baikal holds more fresh water than all five of North America's Great Lakes combined.
